en: Section on Full Understanding 2.3.4. Chapter on the Present and the Past
Is he who fully understands the aggregate of form one who has fully understood the aggregate of feeling? No.
Or again, is he who has fully understood the aggregate of feeling one who fully understands the aggregate of form? No.
Is he who does not fully understand the aggregate of form one who has not fully understood the aggregate of feeling?
An Arahant does not fully understand the aggregate of form, but he has not failed to fully understand the aggregate of feeling.

With the exception of one who possesses the highest path (the Arahant) and the Arahant himself, all remaining persons neither fully understand the aggregate of form nor have they fully understood the aggregate of feeling.
Or, conversely: whoever has not fully understood the aggregate of feeling, does he not fully understand the aggregate of form?
One who possesses the highest path has not fully understood the aggregate of feeling, but does not fail to fully understand the aggregate of form.

With the exception of one who possesses the highest path and an Arahant, all remaining persons have neither fully understood the aggregate of feeling nor do they fully understand the aggregate of form.
